original_value: This paper describes an experience in teaching Machine Learning (ML) and Natural Language Processing (NLP) to a group of high school students over an intense one-month period. In this work, we provide an outline of an AI course curriculum we designed for high school students and then evaluate its effectiveness by analyzing student's feedback and student outcomes. After closely observing students, evaluating their responses to our surveys, and analyzing their contribution to the course project, we identified some possible impediments in teaching AI to high school students and propose some measures to avoid them. These measures include employing a combination of objectivist and constructivist pedagogies, reviewing/introducing basic programming concepts at the beginning of the course, and addressing gender discrepancies throughout the course.

result.paraphrase: This paper presents an intensive one-month teaching experience in Machine Learning (ML) and Natural Language Processing (NLP) with high school students. It outlines the AI course curriculum we created for them and assesses its effectiveness through student feedback and outcomes. By closely observing the students, examining their survey responses, and analyzing their contributions to the course project, we identified potential obstacles to teaching AI to high school students and suggest ways to address them. These include using a mix of objectivist and constructivist pedagogies, revisiting and introducing basic programming concepts at the start of the course, and tackling gender disparities throughout the course.
